decisions.reason: Despite weaker recent visibility, the firm has already invested in a multi-model housing line that fits its integrated drainage system architecture, so management is more likely to continue than to reverse course.
Because floor-level shower drainage sits very close to the firm's stated move toward accessible and low-profile bathroom solutions, strategic fit and prior development spending favor retention.
As a publicly presented flagship for the firm's future direction, this designer drainage line carries the strongest commitment and is therefore least likely to be withdrawn.
The integrated-slope shower element supports installation ease and renovation applications central to the firm's positioning, allowing management to justify continued support.

Although more niche than the shower-focused lines, the prominently launched backflow-protected basement drain embodies specialist engineering investment that a German drainage manufacturer would be reluctant to abandon quickly.
With lower promotional visibility and a weaker connection to the firm's shower-led strategic narrative, the air-admittance valve is the easiest product line to discontinue after several years.
